text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 24 in history.
1401 - In his sweep through Asia and the Mediterranean, the Tatar ruler Tamerlane conquered Damascus.
1449 - England broke a truce and captured Fougeres from the French, leading Charles VII to renew the Hundred Years War.
1603 - Queen Elizabeth I died after ruling England for over 40 years. James VI of Scotland acceded to the throne as James I, uniting the thrones of Scotland and England.
1644 - Britain granted a charter to Roger Williams for the colony of Rhode Island.
1834 - William Morris, poet, artist, designer and early pioneer of British socialism, born.
1882 - Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, U.S. poet and author of "Song of Hiawatha", died.
1887 - Roscoe (Fatty) Arbuckle, U.S. silent film comedian, actor and director, born.
1901 - Ub Iwerks, U.S. animator, born. Instrumental in the creation of Mickey Mouse, he also had credits as special effects expert on such films as Hitchcock's "The Birds"
1905 - Jules Verne, French novelist who wrote "Journey to the Centre of the Earth" and "Around the World in Eighty Days", died at Amiens.
1909 - Clyde Barrow, bank robber and half of the team "Bonnie and Clyde", born.
1909 - John Millington Synge, Irish playwright and leading figure of the Irish literary renaissance, died.
1930 - Steve McQueen,U.S. film actor, born. Best known for his "The Great Escape" and "Bullitt".
1934 - U.S. adopted the Tydings-McDuffie Act providing for Philippines independence in 1945.
1944 - General Orde Wingate was killed in a plane crash in Burma. He had led his "Chindits", a band of British, Gurkha and Burmese guerrillas, in raids behind Japanese lines from 1943-44.
1953 - Queen Mary, wife of King George V, died just three months before the coronation of her granddaughter Elizabeth II.
1953 - A resident of Ten Rillington Place, London, discovered a body in a cupboard. It led to the arrest of mass murderer John Christie.
1958 - Rock and roll star Elvis Presley joined the U.S. army for two years.
1962 - Auguste Piccard, Swiss physicist, deep-sea explorer and balloonist, died. Twin brother of Jean-Felix and member of the famous family of Swiss scholars.
1965 - U.S. spacecraft Ranger 9 crash-landed on the moon. Some of the 5,000 pictures it sent back were broadcast live on TV for the first time.
1976 - President Isabel Peron of Argentina was deposed in a bloodless military coup; Gen. Jorge Videla was named as President.
1976 - Field Marshall Bernard Law Montgomery, 1st Viscount Montgomery of Alamein, died. He defeated the Germans at El Alamein and helped turn the course of World War Two in Africa.
1977 - Morarji Desai was sworn in as India Prime Minister, replacing Indira Gandhi.
1978 - The oil tanker Amoco Cadiz, aground in the English Channel since March 16, split in two spilling the last of her 1.6 million barrels of oil.
1980 - Archbishop Oscar Arnulfo Romero was shot dead by right-wing hit squads while preparing for mass in San Salvador.
1982 - Lt.-Gen Mohammad Hossain Ershad declared himself martial law leader of Bangladesh after a military coup.
1988 - Former nuclear technician Mordechai Vanunu was found guilty in an Israeli court of treason for revealing Israel's nuclear secrets.
1993 - Ezer Weizman was elected Israel's seventh President.
1994 - The self-proclaimed Bosnian Serb republic refused to join a Moslem-Croat federation until U.N. sanctions on Serbia were lifted.
1995 - Britain said it was halting all routine army patrols in Belfast for the first time in 25 years.
1996 - Iraqis voted in the country's first parliamentary elections since the 1991 Gulf War. Most of the candidates registered as independents.
